title: The Peculiar Patriot by Liza Jessie Peterson at New York Theatre Work...
transcript: This performance by Liza Jessie Peterson is so precise and realized, it's as if she's been doing it for 25 years, because she has. In The Peculiar Patriot, she plays a woman named Betsy Laquanda Ross visiting her friend Joann in prison. Over a series of visits, they exchange personal updates, discuss Betsy's dating life, and other people in their circle navigating the legal system. The piece speaks directly to the prison industrial complex, how mass incarceration is used for profit rather than punishment, and how these issues disproportionately impact Black communities, largely by design. While it's not based on one specific person or story, the piece feels documentary-esque in how well-researched it clearly is and in its starkly confessional and direct delivery. Although we spend the majority of the show seeing just one side of these conversations with Betsy sitting at a table, it's absolutely engrossing. Liza has created a complex but endearing and familiar character who's overwhelmingly aware of the injustices her community is subjected to but still overflows with humor and optimism in spite of everything she carries. The way the piece combines detailed characterization with dense information gave me elements of Anna Deveare Smith, but it's a truly singular, funny, and richly layered performance. After taking it to theatres and prisons across the country over the past 25 years, this run marks Liza's final performances of the piece. I would highly recommend getting to New York Theatre Workshop before it closes on June 14th. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer expresses strong enthusiasm throughout, praising the performance as 'engrossing,' 'singular,' and 'richly layered,' and explicitly gives a high recommendation to see it before it closes.
